summary: Snapcast is a multiroom audio server that distributes time-synchronised audio streams to multiple clients over a network. It acts as the central hub for playing coordinated sound across different rooms or hardware targets simultaneously. The system relies on a client-server architecture written in C++ to achieve tight synchronisation.
goodFor: It is a suitable choice if you want to build a custom multiroom audio setup using existing playback hardware without proprietary vendor lock-in.
watchOut: The project shows signs of slowing development activity, which may impact long-term maintenance and compatibility with newer audio backends.
deployNotes: As a compiled C++ application distributed as a deb package, it typically runs as a system daemon without requiring a database or heavy persistent storage. You will need to configure network access and audio inputs properly on the host machine to stream your sources.
